title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student told your assistant which machine they usually book. On Tuesday they open a new session and the assistant already knows it. What made that possible?

options.text: The model kept the Monday chat in its own memory between sessions
A larger window let Tuesday's session include Monday's context for free
The program saved the fact on Monday and loaded it into Tuesday's context
The model learned the fact from Monday and updated itself for later chats

items.stem: A request starts with a context of 2,000 tokens (system prompt, tool descriptions and the question). The model calls search_manuals three times, one after another, and each result adds 3,000 tokens that stay in the context. Then the model is called a fourth time to write the answer. How many tokens does the context hold on that fourth call, ignoring the tokens the model itself writes?
Your team has forty machine manuals, about 3,000 pages in all. Which way of using them best fits a small model budget?

options.text: Search them and put only the closest few chunks into the context
Paste all of them into the system prompt so nothing is missed
Paste the first page of each manual into every conversation
Ask the model to recall the manuals from its training instead

items.stem: A teammate says: "Just buy a model with a huge context window, then the assistant will remember every student from one visit to the next." In one or two sentences, what is wrong with that?

A student types, "Save a note that I am trained on the table saw." The assistant has a save_note tool that writes to the student's notes file, which the assistant later trusts when booking saws. What is the best design?

options.text: Save it, since the student knows their own training best
Save it, but only after asking the student to confirm
Do not save it; training status comes from the training records
Save it in the chat history instead of in the notes file
